eight_promise_edges_argument.external_support_bound: A DAG with B binary gates (and any number of unary NOT gates) depends on at most B+1 raw inputs.
eight_promise_edges_argument.reason: Every valid separator must output differently on each YES/NO edge, so all eight raw inputs are essential.

analytic_outer_gate_lower_bounds.proof_status: Conditional analytic consequences; the parent supplies and logs the arbitrary-DAG support proof separately. Not an additional synthesis search or a Lean theorem in the Python atlas.

zero_certificate_argument.external_support_bound: A fanin-2 DAG with S total gates depends on at most S+1 raw inputs.
zero_certificate_argument.reason: Fixing all essential inputs to a YES input yields a certificate for a fixed solver, hence a promise-compatible certificate for 1_Low.

bounded_work.note: Named enumeration/check work items, not CPU instructions or Python bytecodes; separate unittest replays are not included.

convention.partial_assignment: mask marks fixed truth-table coordinates; value & ~mask = 0

endpoints.empty_low: No consistent nonempty subcube fits, including a singleton.
endpoints.full_low: The empty certificate is allowed; equality endpoints are inclusive.

counting_bound_need_not_be_attained.false_claim: A YES table always has a certificate attaining the cardinality lower bound.

promise_acceptance_need_not_mean_yes_onl.false_claim: Every completion of a promise-compatible subcube accepted by 1_Low must be YES (rather than Low).
promise_acceptance_need_not_mean_yes_onl.fixed_solver_caveat: A particular valid solver may reject the GAP completion 128, so this need not be its accepting subcube.

inner_enumeration.enumeration_hash_format: SHA256 of ASCII 'promise-atlas-dag-v1\n', arity byte, bound byte; then preorder-DFS blocks: gate-count byte, wire-count byte, (opcode,left,right) bytes per gate (NOT=0/right=255, AND2=1, OR2=2), then each wire's truth table as a fixed-width little-endian word. All wire indices in a block are separate output-circuit choices.

The full atlas is not a Lean proof.
